SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) champion seed points so far: seed42(iter-12) 0.8638; seed43(iter-14) 0.7983. iter-14 log CONFIRMS all 5 epochs completed (loss 1e-6, 'Time limit reached AT epoch 5' fired only after ep5 finished) -> the 0.064 swing is a GENUINE seed effect, NOT budget truncation. (2) FAILURE MODE: the champion is SEED-SENSITIVE (spread 0.8638 vs 0.7983 across two seeds) -- likely the val_n=200 noise floor compounded with end-to-end unrolled-training run-to-run variance. iter-14's falsifier (swing>0.02) FIRED -> must widen the replicate set to characterize the true mean+/-std before reporting a champion number. (3) ONE KNOB: seed 43 -> 44 (3rd seed point). (4) HYPOTHESIS: seed 44 lands somewhere in [0.79, 0.87]; three points (42,43,44) let me compute a provisional mean+/-std and see whether 0.8638 was a favorable-seed high or the norm. FALSIFIER: n/a for a replicate -- this is variance characterization; the outcome (wherever it lands) refines the spread. (5) BUDGET (HARD 20min=1200s): identical config to iter-12/14 except seed; both prior runs completed all 5 epochs (iter-12 1190.98s, iter-14 finished ep5 then the 1130s fence tripped). max_train_s raised to 1140 so a fast-enough node completes ep5 cleanly and a slow node still lands val+figure inside the 30-min sbatch wall on the fully-or-nearly-trained model -> valid numeric-headroom obs either way. train_n=2400 (<= OOM-safe cap). val=200 distinct val_truth.h5 cases, 256px inscribed-circle FOV (breast default). (6) do NOT return control mid-campaign; gate on iter-15 numeric-headroom obs via iter_wait.sh v3 then dispatch iter-16.
